title: Channel fallback strategies and SLO weighting notes
body:
Context:
This is a working brain-dump for a compact UX for: 1) composing alert/notification policies tied to SLOs, 2) multi-channel fallback strategies, and 3) a simple SLO-weighting model that surfaces recommended thresholds and expected alert volumes. Goal: give oncall owners predictable noisy/valuable signal tradeoffs and an easy way to simulate the impact of policy changes before rollout.

High-level requirements (assumptions):
- Users want to author a single policy that can fan out to multiple channels with priorities and fallbacks, not create separate per-channel rules.
- SLO-derived thresholds: system should suggest thresholds (p95/p99, error-rate, latency) based on historical windows and SLO weight (critical/secondary).
- Lightweight simulation/dry-run to estimate monthly alert volume and cost (SMS/phone expensive).
- Support schedule-aware routing (primary team oncall -> escalation -> external pager channel).
- Integration: Slack, PagerDuty, Email, SMS, Webhook.

Suggested UX primitives / wireframe notes:
1) Policy Composer canvas (left-to-right):
   - Top bar: policy name, linked SLO(s) dropdown, quick preview of expected alert rate (calc).
   - Central canvas: a linear chain of "channel cards" representing priority lanes (primary -> secondary -> escalate). Each card shows channel type, target (Slack #ops), delay before send (0s / 2m / 10m), and a small cost badge.
   - Channel card controls: priority weight slider (0-100), severity multiplier (info/warn/critical), mute windows (quiet hours per recipient), conditional expression toggle (advanced).
   - Right rail: simulation panel with sample traffic (last 30d) and projected alerts given current thresholds. Toggle between realistic/historic/random traffic.

2) Threshold editor (modal):
   - Linked to SLO: offer three presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with sample expected alert volume and impact.
   - Show how each preset maps to numeric thresholds, e.g., latency p95 > 1.2s or error_rate > 0.5%.
   - Inline examples: "If SLO 99.9% availability, recommend error_rate threshold = 0.1% (conservative)".

3) SLO Weighting concept (simple):
   - Each SLO can be tagged with a weight label: critical(100), important(60), minor(20). When composing multi-SLO policy, combine weights to suggest a composite threshold and recommended channels (critical->pager, important->Slack, minor->email).
   - Expose an override on policy to treat one SLO as "dominant" for threshold decisions.

4) Fallback logic examples:
   - Immediate fanout: send to all channels concurrently (useful for widespread outages).
   - Priority fallback: send to channel A immediately; if no ack within X minutes escalate to channel B.
   - Cost-aware fallback: avoid SMS for "info" severity; only use SMS for critical after 2 escalations.
   - Region-aware routing: prefer regional paging endpoints; fallback to global when regional offline.

Backlog / grooming items (atomic tickets):
- CRT-3001: Implement channel card UI + priority slider (acceptance: add/modify channel, change delay, preview cost).
- CRT-3002: Threshold presets and SLO weight integration (acceptance: policies can link to SLOs and auto-populate threshold suggestions).
- CRT-3003: Simulation engine (acceptance: simulate 30d historic traffic and produce an alert volume estimate + cost estimate).
- CRT-3004: Schedule-aware routing UI and test harness (acceptance: team schedules respected; escalations follow schedule).
- CRT-3005: Export policy to JSON + backend schema (acceptance: roundtrip save/load).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How opinionated should default SLO weights be? Risk: too prescriptive frustrates platform teams. Proposal: ship with reasonable defaults and a quick "tuning" walkthrough.
- Cost estimates accuracy: we can provide ranges until we have tokenized SMS/email billing. Start with conservative/median estimates.
- Conditional expressions: full boolean builders vs. lightweight toggles. Start with a simple 'AND/OR' builder + common templates, defer full expression language.
- Acknowledgement model: should a Slack thread ack suppress escalation? (Yes, but define time window and explicit ack button).

Sample user flows (short):
- Flow A (oncall focused): Ops lead links SLOs for infra cluster -> picks "balanced" preset -> composes channels: Slack->PagerDuty(2m)->SMS(10m only if PD unacked) -> runs simulation -> saves and enables policy in canary mode for 24h.
- Flow B (cost-sensitive): Platform eng marks SLO as "minor" -> selects "aggressive" (fewer alerts) -> channels Email->Slack (no SMS) -> simulation shows low monthly alert cost -> enable.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- Users can link 1+ SLO to a policy and get suggested numeric thresholds.
- Users can attach 2+ channels with configurable delay and priority and save the policy.
- Basic simulation returns projected alert volumes with a simple cost estimate.
- Policy can be toggled to dry-run (notifications not sent, but logs produced).

Next steps / owners:
- UX: produce 3 small wireframes (Priya, due 2025-11-18).
- Backend: schema for policy + simulation endpoint (Luca, prototype by 2025-12-01).
- Integrations: list exact fields needed for PagerDuty/Slack/SMS (Diego, doc by 2025-11-25).

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep composer horizontal and scannable. Channel cost should be visible but collapsible.
- Add a "why did this fire" link on each simulated alert pointing to the SLO metric slice.
- For rollout, include a canary mode that only notifies a subset of recipients or logs to a sandbox channel.

End of notes.
